statement: Magyar cavalry raids devastated East Francia repeatedly from 899 to 955, penetrating as far as Burgundy, Lorraine, Saxony, and Italy. The raids — lightning fast, burning crops and towns, returning before resistance could organize — exposed the inadequacy of Carolingian defense. The Saxon kings Henry I 'the Fowler' organized systematic counter-measures: building burgs (fortified towns), training heavy cavalry, and negotiating a 9-year truce (926–934) that bought time. His son Otto I finally crushed the Magyars at the Battle of Lechfeld (955), ending the raids and demonstrating German military superiority that enabled Otto's imperial coronation (962).
